challengeFindings.title: A code agent writes a planned test whose red recorded its file `missing`, and every code step now lets it through without a refusal or a `changedTests` record
A later code step puts a `BLOCKED`-changed test back as the tests step wrote it, is refused, and the re-ask tells it to do what it already did
A re-asked code agent re-appends the `BLOCKED` line with a reason already recorded for the test, the engine skips it without saying why, and the run takes the Failure Path
A `BLOCKED` test line whose `— {why}` is only whitespace lets the change through with an empty reason, so the owner is asked about it with no reason
A `--field 'changedTests=[…]'` on any `steps finish` re-baselines a planned test with no `BLOCKED` line, and a record with no reason never appears in `changed`, so the owner is never asked
A code step's `BLOCKED` change to a test whose red was never proven (`vacuous`, `lint`) records it as `state: "red"`, and `tests red` then treats the test as proven and never runs it again
A code agent deletes a planned test's assertions, logs a plausible `BLOCKED` reason, and the weakened test merges, because the owner only ever sees the agent's own words

challengeFindings.title: In a repo with no `bkit:test:file` script, a code agent keeps a planned-test change under a `BLOCKED` line and it merges unseen, because `tests green` prints `changed: []` whenever test-first is not enforced
A later group's tests step adds a test to a file whose earlier-group planned test has no recorded block, and every later code step is refused with exit 11 that no `BLOCKED` line can clear
A `changedTests` record on any step row, written through `--field changedTests=...` or with no reason, moves the lock's baseline, and `tests green` then hides it from the owner
A code agent writes a planned test whole, after its red recorded the file `missing`, under a `BLOCKED` line, and the owner's `CHANGED_TESTS` item carries no diff, only the agent's reason
A code agent logs `BLOCKED - TASK 3: test ...` with a hyphen, the lock lets the change through, and the build summary still lists task 3 as blocked after its `DONE — TASK 3` line
A `BLOCKED` line names a changed test by the last ` > ` segment of a name that itself holds `>` (for example `keeps a >= 0`), and the step is refused
A `BLOCKED` test line whose reason is only a trailing space (an `echo` with an empty variable) lets the change through with an empty reason, and the owner's item says nothing about why
A code agent adds one `return;` line before a planned test's assertions, logs a `BLOCKED` reason, and the engine lets the disabled test through as "additive", while verify only notes it
